In MCUboot's serial-recovery encrypted-image support (boot/boot_serial/src/boot_serial_encryption.c), decrypt_image_inplace() and boot_image_validate_encrypted() each keep a stack-local struct boot_status. boot_enc_load() writes the plaintext per-image AES key into its enckey[] field. Neither function cleared this structure before returning. In addition, a decrypt failure inside the per-sector loop of decrypt_image_inplace() returned early and skipped the total_out: cleanup, which left the expanded AES key context (enc_data) on the stack as well. The error paths of boot_image_validate_encrypted() similarly skipped boot_enc_zeroize().

The affected code is built when encrypted images (MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES, Zephyr CONFIG_BOOT_ENCRYPT_IMAGE) are combined with serial recovery. It runs when an encrypted image is uploaded to the primary slot over the recovery protocol, and when the image list or state is queried while an encrypted image is in the secondary slot. After these functions return, the image's AES content key remains in dead stack memory. An attacker who can later read device RAM, for example through a debug port or retained RAM, can recover it.

This weakens the confidentiality of image-encryption keys within the bootloader trust boundary. A recovered key exposes the plaintext of the encrypted firmware image it protects. The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed. No remote or recovery-protocol channel that returns this memory is known, so exploitation requires a separate memory-read capability.

A pull request review created through the API as a draft (`event` set to `PENDING` or left empty) was added to the pull request timeline and announced through notifications and activity feeds like a submitted review. Its body and line comments were therefore visible to everyone who can read the pull request, including anonymous visitors of a public repository, before the reviewer submitted it. Pending reviews no longer get a timeline entry or notifications until they are submitted.

FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains a use-after-free vulnerability that leaves a dangling pointer to a freed environment table when putenv() is called during request shutdown. Attackers triggering putenv() in shutdown functions, destructors, or session handlers can crash the process on the next getenv() call or leak previous request environment values.

FrankenPHP before 1.13.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in worker mode that leaks per-request environment variables into later requests on the same PHP thread. Attackers can read values set via env directives with request placeholders or WithRequestEnv() through getenv() or $_SERVER, causing applications to act on another user's routing, tenant, or authorization values.

FrankenPHP before 1.13.0 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to spoof trusted headers by sending dot-form header names that PHP rewrites to underscores. Attackers can send headers like X.Authenticated.User or X.Forwarded.For that map to $_SERVER keys, spoofing user identity, client IP, or scheme.

FrankenPHP Docker images before 1.1.11 were rebuilt only when new base image tags were created, so security fixes that Alpine, PHP, and Go applied under existing tags were not propagated. Remote attackers could exploit known flaws in the stale system libraries, such as CVE-2025-15467 in libcrypto3, to execute code.

OpenMage magento-lts before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an incorrect authorization vulnerability because admin controllers' _isAllowed() checks fall back to, or only check, parent ACL resources instead of finer per-action permissions. Authenticated restricted administrators can mass cancel or hold orders, rewrite order shipping addresses, export customer report data, or create REST roles despite their role denying those permissions.

In gittuf before 0.18.0, verification of file protection rules uses the quoted, escaped pathnames that Git prints by default for files with special characters (for example non-ASCII characters) instead of the raw paths. Such paths do not match patterns like file:internal/*, so the files are treated as unprotected, and a user who is not authorized by a file protection rule can change a protected file whose name contains special characters and still pass verification.

In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.17.0, the verification workflow does not load policy updates that are propagated from an upstream (controller) repository and recorded in the reference state log after the first entry being verified. Only the propagated policy in effect at the start of verification is applied, so later controller changes to global rules, such as threshold requirements and force-push blocks, are ignored and changes that these rules should block pass verification.

In gittuf 0.4.0 through 0.16.0, when a policy update appears within the range of reference state log entries being verified, verification checks only the root of trust signatures of the new policy and not the signatures of its other metadata (rule files). A user trusted to push to the repository who bypasses gittuf policy apply and writes the policy reference and reference state log directly can make an invalid policy apply during verification, weakening or strengthening the rules for later changes. The update is still recorded in the reference state log.

In gittuf 0.10.0 through 0.15.0, when a minimum threshold global rule and a policy rule protect the same namespace, verification gives the global rule's check over all trusted users in the policy precedence over the policy rule's own authorized users. A user listed in the policy file but not authorized by the policy rule, or fewer users than the rule's threshold, can make changes to the protected namespace that pass verification.

The All in One SEO – AI SEO Plugin to Boost SEO Rankings & Traffic (Schema, Local SEO, Sitemap & SEO Insights) plugin for WordPress is vulnerable to Stored Cross-Site Scripting via the 'name' parameter in all versions up to, and including, 5.0.5 due to insufficient input sanitization and output escaping. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with subscriber-level access and above, to inject arbitrary web scripts in pages that will execute whenever a user accesses an injected page. Successful exploitation requires that an administrator has placed the AIOSEO breadcrumb on the author template, that the site is running WordPress 6.6 or later with the core Interactivity runtime loaded (e.g., via a block theme or core/navigation block), and that a victim clicks the rendered breadcrumb link on the author archive page.

OpenMage Magento-LTS before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains an authorization bypass in the /rss/order/status feed because its URL key is unsigned Base64-encoded JSON of the order, increment, and customer ids. Unauthenticated attackers can forge keys from enumerated sequential ids to read other customers' names, items, prices, totals, and status comments when order-status RSS is enabled.

OpenMage Magento LTS before 20.18.2 and 21.0.0-beta1 before 21.0.0-beta3 contains a cross-site request forgery vulnerability in the admin and storefront OAuth confirm and confirmSimple actions, which accept GET requests without form-key validation. Attackers holding OAuth consumer credentials can lure a logged-in administrator or customer to a crafted confirm URL that authorizes the attacker's request token, then exchange it at /oauth/token for a persistent REST API access token bound to the victim.

Nuxt is an open-source web development framework for Vue.js. From @nuxt/webpack-builder 3.0.0 and @nuxt/rspack-builder 3.12.2 until 4.6.4, the development middleware trusts Origin, Referer, or Sec-Fetch-Site when the Host header names the same attacker-controlled hostname. After DNS rebinding changes that hostname to a loopback address, a malicious page opened by a developer can read /_nuxt/*.js client chunks and inline source maps, exposing compiled application source, local filesystem paths, and developer-controlled values embedded in the client bundle. The attacker must know or guess the development-server port and induce the developer to open the malicious page; Chrome 142 and later and other Chromium-based browsers that enforce Local Network Access restrictions prompt before a public page can reach the loopback address. The default Vite builder and production builds are unaffected. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.4.

When MCUboot is built with the TinyCrypt crypto backend (MCUBOOT_USE_TINYCRYPT), bootutil_aes_ctr_drop() in boot/bootutil/include/bootutil/crypto/aes_ctr_tinycrypt.h was an empty stub. The AES-CTR context for this backend is the fully expanded AES-128 key schedule (struct tc_aes_key_sched_struct). Generic code relies on this hook to release and clear key state, so with TinyCrypt nothing was cleared. The mbedTLS and PSA backends do free or destroy their key state here.

As a result, boot_state_clear(), which boot_go() calls before handing off to the application, left the image's AES content-encryption key schedule in the static boot_data state. This is the case after an encrypted upgrade in single-image builds, where boot_enc_zeroize() is not called. boot_decrypt_key() likewise left the ECIES-derived key-encryption key schedule on the stack. The affected build uses MCUBOOT_ENC_IMAGES with TinyCrypt, which is the default ECDSA and Ed25519 backend in the Zephyr port.

The first AES-128 round key equals the cipher key, so anyone who can read the leftover bootloader RAM after boot can recover the image content key and decrypt that encrypted image. That includes a physical attacker with debug or RAM access, or code later running on the device. This weakens image-encryption key confidentiality (and so the confidentiality of the encrypted image's plaintext). The device's long-term private decryption key is not exposed, and image authenticity is not affected. The fix wipes the context with bootutil_wipe_memory().

SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. From version 2.60.1 until 3.1.1, applications using the experimental remote functions flag could assign the same generated identifier to separate non-exported query.batch functions. When those private functions shared a request batch, arguments intended for one function could be passed to another function, causing unexpected cross-function processing and possible disclosure of function arguments. This issue is fixed in 3.1.1.

SvelteKit is a framework for rapidly developing robust, performant web applications using Svelte. From version 5.5.7 until versions 5.5.8 and 6.0.1, , @sveltejs/adapter-node can attempt to add a header to an immutable request in a context that causes the server to crash, denying service to any other requests routed to that server. This issue is fixed in 5.5.8 and 6.0.1.

NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.parse.dependencygraph.dot2img resolves the Graphviz dot executable through PATH but invokes the resulting absolute executable without routing through spawn_trusted, so resolve_trusted_executable ownership and writability validation and safe_env loader environment scrubbing do not run. A local low-privileged attacker who can write to a directory on a POSIX victim's PATH can plant or replace dot, and code executes as the victim when dot2img is called directly or DependencyGraph.repr_svg renders a graph. The current-working-directory-only bare-name vector is blocked and is not this vulnerability; this issue is the residual writable absolute PATH element bypass after CVE-2026-78680. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

Scapy before 2.8.0 contains a denial of service vulnerability in BER_num_dec() and BERcodec_OID.do_dec() that allows remote attackers to exhaust CPU by supplying oversized OID arcs. Attackers can send ASN.1/BER data with many base-128 continuation bytes to cause quadratic CPU consumption or an uncaught ValueError crash on Python 3.11+.

The xmlwf tool in libexpat through 2.10.0 contains a symlink following vulnerability because -d output mode opens files with fopen("wb"), which follows symbolic links. Local attackers with write access to the output directory can plant a symlink at the expected output name to truncate or overwrite files writable by the xmlwf user.

Tight JPEG decoding in TightVNC and UltraVNC viewers contains a heap-based buffer overflow because an attacker-controlled framebuffer rectangle width is not validated against a fixed-size decoding buffer. A malicious VNC server can cause an out-of-bounds heap write when a user connects, resulting in application crash and potentially other memory-corruption impacts.

Miniflux before 2.3.5 contains an insufficient session expiration vulnerability that allows attackers to retain account access because password changes do not revoke existing web sessions. Attackers holding a leaked password or copied session cookie keep access for up to 30 days, reading integration credentials, creating API keys, or registering passkeys.

listmonk 6.2.0 before 7.0.0-beta.2 contains a missing authentication vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to submit Azure Event Grid bounce webhooks when no shared secret is configured. Attackers can POST forged EmailDeliveryReportReceived events with Bounced status to /webhooks/service/azure to blocklist, unsubscribe, or delete arbitrary subscribers.

When Gitea acts as an OAuth2 or OpenID Connect provider, the token endpoint did not check the state of the user. After an administrator deactivated an account or prohibited its sign-in, existing refresh tokens and unused authorization codes of that user could still be exchanged for new tokens, so applications that sign users in through Gitea kept them signed in. The token endpoint now refuses users who may not sign in, and token introspection reports their tokens as inactive.

Removing a team's review request looked up a review by the negated team ID, which for the team with ID 2 is the ID of the built-in Actions user, and marked the review it found as official. In the organization that owns that team, a user who can change the review requests of a pull request could make an approval left by the Actions user count toward the approvals required by branch protection. Merging still required permission to merge. Removing a team review request no longer changes any review.

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.2, ABAC-enabled deployments of the Submodel Repository and the AAS Environment do not apply an access rule's `FILTERLIST` fragment filters to single Submodel reads.



`GET /submodels` removes the fields that a rule's `FILTERLIST` hides, but `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}` and `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$metadata` return them unfiltered. An authenticated caller with READ access to a Submodel can therefore read fields that the access rules hide from them, for example `supplementalSemanticIds` keys that name the other parties allowed to read the Submodel.



If versioning is enabled (`history.mode` set to `api` or `audit`), `GET /submodels/{submodelIdentifier}/$history` and `GET /shells/{aasIdentifier}/$history` in the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment return the complete stored version without applying the rule's formula or fragment filters. A caller whose rules grant READ on these routes can read fields that the access rules hide, and Submodels and Asset Administration Shells that the direct read does not return to them at all.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.3.

A flaw was found in Red Hat Quay. The v1 registry API error handler reflects the attacker-supplied image_id path segment in a response served as text/html, allowing a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack. By tricking a user into visiting a specially crafted URL, a remote attacker can execute arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser within the Quay origin, potentially compromising the user's session.

** UNSUPPORTED WHEN ASSIGNED ** Missing authentication for critical function vulnerability in Apache Griffin Web Service. The REST API does not have any authentication. This includes sensitive endpoints, such as job submission when a Livy/Spark backend is configured. The API must be properly secured on the network level, and this fact was arguably not documented as clearly as it could have.



This issue affects Apache Griffin Web Service: all versions.



As this project is retired, we do not plan to release a version that fixes this issue. Users are recommended to find an alternative or restrict access to the instance to trusted users.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer.

@fastify/busboy is a streaming parser for multipart form data used by Fastify. In versions 3.2.1 through 3.2.5, the parser can interpret the same multipart bytes differently depending on how they are split across socket reads: when the sequence that terminates a part's header block arrives split exactly at the configured header size limit, an off by one error drops the final header line, so a part declared as a binary file attachment is emitted as an ordinary text field instead of a file. A remote client controls both the multipart body and the header padding needed to reach the boundary and can influence segmentation, so an application that applies upload validation such as malware scanning or extension checks only to file events while trusting plain field values may process the payload through the wrong path. The parser level type confusion is fully reproducible, while the downstream validation bypass depends on the application. The issue is fixed in @fastify/busboy 3.2.6, which tracks how many terminator bytes were actually buffered when the limit is reached so a split terminator no longer corrupts the final header, and users should upgrade to 3.2.6 or later. As a workaround, apply the same validation to field values as to file uploads rather than treating file events as a trust boundary.

Missing authentication for a critical function (CWE-306) in the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to read device information, such as the serial number, MAC address, IP address and radio configuration, and to change configuration settings. The service accepts commands in DJI's proprietary DUML protocol without any authentication. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The same commands are also accepted over the USB operator port. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

OS command injection (CWE-78) in the network-configuration handling of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to execute arbitrary commands as root. Configuration values that can be written without authentication over the management interface are inserted unquoted into shell commands. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. The injected command persists across reboots. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

Improper verification of cryptographic signature (CWE-347) in the firmware update handler of the management service (uavmonitor_usbv1) of the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an unauthenticated attacker on the local network to install modified firmware, which gives persistent code execution as root. The device accepts any image that matches an MD5 checksum supplied in the same request and does not verify a signature. Exploitation requires network access to TCP port 16000 on the board and that the unit is not connected to another controlling host. Reproduced by running the unmodified device binaries in emulation; not tested on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

Use of hard-coded credentials (CWE-798) on the 1300 communications board in DJI AeroScope Mobile (TP703) firmware 03.00.00.26, with 1300 communications board firmware 02.00.07.12 through 02.00.08.40, allows an attacker with physical access to the board's serial console to log in as root. The same password hash is present on every unit and uses DES crypt, so the password can be recovered offline from the distributed firmware. No network login service accepts this password by default. Confirmed on a physical device.



NOTE: This vulnerability only affects products that are no longer supported by the maintainer. DJI has discontinued AeroScope Mobile and no fixed firmware is available.

In Eclipse BaSyx Go Components versions up to and including 1.1.3, ABAC-enabled deployments match `ROUTE` access rules against the fully decoded request path, while the router routes on the raw, still encoded path. An encoded slash (`%2F`) inside a path value is a segment separator for the access check but part of the value for the router, so a request can match a narrow `ROUTE` rule while the handler returns a different, larger resource.



An authenticated caller whose rules grant READ only on parts of a resource can therefore read the whole resource. In the DPP API, a rule such as `/v1/dpps/*/elements/*`, meant to grant only passport elements, also grants the complete passport whose identifier contains `/elements/`. In the Submodel Repository, AAS Repository and AAS Environment, a rule such as `/submodels/*/submodel-elements/*/attachment`, meant to grant only file attachments, also grants the complete element whose stored idShort contains `%2F`.



The issue is fixed in Eclipse BaSyx Go Components v1.1.4.

A flaw was found in dbus. A local attacker can exploit this vulnerability by connecting to an affected service, requesting a response, and stopping socket reads while keeping the connection open. Because the socket transport handles broken pipe write errors as retryable, the application enters a continuous retry loop. This can lead to excessive CPU consumption, resulting in a denial of service (DoS) for the target process.

xschem 2.9.9 through 3.4.7 contains a heap out-of-bounds write vulnerability in read_dataset() in src/rawtovcd.c due to an unchecked variable index. Attackers can supply a crafted ngspice .raw file that, when converted with rawtovcd, writes file-controlled heap pointers at chosen signed offsets, corrupting heap memory.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Very Good Plugins WP Fusion Lite wp-fusion-lite allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP Fusion Lite: from n/a through 3.48.0.

Improper Neutralization of Script-Related HTML Tags in a Web Page (Basic XSS) vulnerability in Automattic WP Job Manager wp-job-manager allows Code Injection.This issue affects WP Job Manager: from n/a through 2.4.10.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WPExperts Gutena Forms – Contact Form, Survey Form, Feedback Form, Booking Form, and Custom Form Builder gutena-forms allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Gutena Forms – Contact Form, Survey Form, Feedback Form, Booking Form, and Custom Form Builder: from n/a through 2.1.1.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in LeapWorx Premium Addons for Elementor premium-addons-for-elementor allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Premium Addons for Elementor: from n/a through 4.11.118.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in Gora Tech Cooked cooked allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects Cooked: from n/a through 1.17.0.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in YITH YITH WooCommerce Product Add-Ons yith-woocommerce-product-add-ons allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects YITH WooCommerce Product Add-Ons: from n/a through 4.35.0.

Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in Cool Plugins Conditional Fields for Elementor Form – Display Conditions conditional-fields-for-elementor-form allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Conditional Fields for Elementor Form – Display Conditions: from n/a through 1.7.7.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in weDevs WP User Frontend wp-user-frontend allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP User Frontend: from n/a through 4.3.14.
Missing Authorization vulnerability in weDevs WP ERP erp allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects WP ERP: from n/a through 1.17.11.

Missing Authorization vulnerability in Crocoblock JetFormBuilder jetformbuilder allows Exploiting Incorrectly Configured Access Control Security Levels.This issue affects JetFormBuilder: from n/a through 3.6.8.1.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to run root commands by importing a malicious OpenVPN client configuration. Attackers can include tls-verify or ipchange directives, which the incomplete denylist does not filter, to execute commands as root when the router connects to an attacker-controlled VPN endpoint.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by uploading crafted OpenVPN private or tls-auth keys. Attackers can close the inline key block with </key>, inject directives such as tls-verify that bypass the .ovpn denylist, and have OpenVPN execute the hook as root.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by injecting newlines into the IPsec keyexchange field of the vpn.set_conf RPC method. Attackers can append a second leftupdown directive to ipsec.conf, which StrongSwan's updown plugin runs as root when an attacker-controlled peer establishes the CHILD_SA.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to execute commands as root by injecting newlines into reboot_time. Attackers can submit a reboot_time value followed by a newline and crontab line, which /etc/init.d/autoreboot writes to the root crontab for crond to run.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a dnsmasq configuration injection vulnerability that allows authenticated administrators to inject directives by embedding a newline in the net.set_dhcp leasetime field. Attackers can append address= entries via /etc/init.d/dnsmasq to alter DNS answers for LAN clients, or insert invalid lines that stop dnsmasq.

JSON::XS versions from 4.0_00 before 4.05 for Perl corrupt the incremental buffer length by chopping past its end in incr_skip after a top-level number.

The incremental parser scans any run of digits, signs, dots and exponent markers as one number, but the decoder stops at the end of a valid number, so the parser keeps an offset into bytes it has not decoded. It then empties the buffer without clearing those bytes, and a later incr_parse call without new input reads them again and moves the offset past the end of the buffer. incr_skip, the documented recovery after an error, removes that many bytes and the buffer length wraps.

A peer sending input such as "1-2" to an incr_parse consumer can make the next read of incr_text exit the process through perl's uncatchable out-of-memory path.

JSON::XS versions from 3.04 before 4.05 for Perl write one byte past a heap buffer when appending a one-byte chunk in incr_parse.

The incremental buffer grows to one and a half times the length it must hold, with no room reserved for the terminating NUL. For an empty buffer and a one-byte chunk that request is one byte, which a buffer whose front was removed by earlier decodes can already have, so nothing is reallocated and the NUL lands one byte past the allocation.

A peer streaming data to an incr_parse consumer, choosing how the input is split into reads, can cause a one-byte heap out-of-bounds write.

JSON::XS versions from 3.0 before 4.05 for Perl read freed stack memory when a FREEZE result's serialisation grows the Perl stack under allow_tags in encode_rv.

With allow_tags, an object's FREEZE method is called in list context and each returned value is encoded through a saved Perl stack pointer. When encoding a returned value calls back into Perl, through TO_JSON under convert_blessed or another FREEZE, and that callback grows the stack, the stack is reallocated while the saved pointer still refers to the freed block.

Encoding such objects reads freed memory, and encode can return undef without an error.

C-Kermit 8.0.200 before 11.1.515 contains an improper certificate hostname validation vulnerability that allows attackers to impersonate hosts by abusing wildcard matching in dNSName_cmp() in ck_ssl.c. Attackers holding a trusted certificate with over-matching names containing asterisks, question marks, brackets, or empty labels can intercept credentials and data over Telnet, FTP, and HTTP TLS connections.

C-Kermit 6.0.192 before 11.1.515 contains a buffer overflow vulnerability in tn_snenv() in ckctel.c that allows malicious Telnet servers to corrupt client memory via crafted NEW-ENVIRON SEND subnegotiation. Malicious or machine-in-the-middle servers can send oversized variable names before authentication, overflowing a 16-byte stack buffer and a miscomputed heap buffer to corrupt stack and heap memory.

C-Kermit before 11.1.515 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in putsrv() in ckcfns.c that allows malicious peers to write past the srvcmd buffer by sending crafted packets. Attackers can use Kermit repeat-count compression in server command, GET, or file-header packets to write attacker-chosen bytes beyond the heap buffer on servers or receiving instances.

Goose CLI 1.35.0 before 1.53.0 contains a local code execution vulnerability that allows attackers to run commands by setting diff.external in a repository's .git/config. Attackers can ship a crafted repository that, when the victim runs goose review, executes git diff without --no-ext-diff, running commands as the user and exposing credentials and provider API keys.

agent-device from 0.21.36 before 0.21.37 contains a local file disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated remote callers to read daemon-host files by opening file:// URLs. Attackers can send an open command with a file:// target through /rpc, then issue snapshot to read any plaintext file readable by the daemon account.

Incorrect default permissions in the agent configuration folder in Devolutions PowerShell Universal 2026.3.4 and earlier allows a local unprivileged user to execute arbitrary code as SYSTEM via a crafted agent configuration file that points the agent to an attacker-controlled server.

paicoding from commit b8206b9 through commit 903adce uses predictable credentials for accounts created via ZSXQ login, because loginByZsxq derives both the username and password solely from the member's ZSXQ number. Unauthenticated attackers can read that number from the victim's /user/{userId} profile page, compute the credentials, and log in via /login/username to take over the account.

paicoding 1.0.0 through 1.0.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because SeoInjectService embeds user profile text without escaping in an inline JSON-LD script element. Authenticated attackers can add a closing script tag followed by HTML to their profile, executing scripts for visitors of their profile page and stealing the non-HttpOnly f-session cookie.

paicoding 1.0.3 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the ArticleRestController article detail endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to read restricted articles. Attackers can enumerate article IDs via GET /article/api/data/detail/{articleId} to retrieve full content of paid, login-only, member-only and draft articles.

SurveyKing 1.12.0 through 1.13.2 contains an authorization bypass in the linked survey feature that fails to verify the referenced linkSurveyId belongs to the caller's own project. Authenticated attackers can point a linked option at another user's survey so that loadLinkResult and updateLinkSurveyAnswer read, rewrite, or create responses in that survey.

DjangoBlog 2.0.0.0 through 2.1.0.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability because the class_filter comment sanitizer passes event-handler attributes on span, div, pre and code tags. Authenticated commenters can post a div with autofocus and onfocus attributes, executing script without interaction for every visitor, including administrators.

ragent 1.0.0 through 1.1.0 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in RagTraceController that allows any logged-in user to view all users' RAG traces. Attackers can page through /rag/traces/runs and related node endpoints to read other users' usernames, user ids, conversation ids, questions, and per-node execution details.

free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in FileShareServiceImpl.getPages, which passes the orderBy parameter of the /apis/share/pages endpoint verbatim into the ORDER BY clause via MyBatis-Flex without a column whitelist. Authenticated users can supply CASE WHEN subquery expressions that use share ordering as a boolean oracle to read arbitrary database contents, such as share codes.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in FileStreamController.preview that allows unauthenticated attackers to download stored files. Attackers who obtain a file ID from share listings or preview links can request /api/file/stream/preview/{fileId} to download any user's or workspace's files.

Dromara free-fs 2.0.1 through 2.3.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability that allows attackers to access code-protected shares because share codes are enforced only client-side. Attackers knowing a share ID can call the share items and download endpoints to list and download files without the code, even on preview-only shares.

Keep 0.34.10 through 0.55.0 contains a blind SQL injection vulnerability in its CEL-to-SQL converter, which inserts bracket-indexed JSON keys from CEL filters unescaped into JSON path expressions for SQLite, PostgreSQL, and MySQL. Authenticated users with read:alert permission can submit crafted CEL expressions to /alerts/query or the cel parameter of /incidents, using result counts as a boolean oracle to extract other tenants' alerts and password hashes.

EdgeEver 1.9.0 before 2.13.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability in the backup restore endpoint PUT /api/v1/restores/json/resources/:id, which accepts a resource kind of image paired with a text/html MIME type without checking consistency. Authenticated members can share the note and send the public blob link to a victim, whose browser executes the script to mint a non-expiring API token granting read and write access to the victim's notes.

A vulnerability has been found in projectworlds Visitor Management System 1.0. This issue affects the function mysqli_query of the file /img/user%20page.php of the component Login Endpoint. Such manipulation of the argument Username leads to sql injection. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit has been disclosed to the public and may be used.

Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the download_file tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go accepts caller-controlled path and dest values, fetches a selected Kubeshark Hub API response, and writes the returned bytes through os.Create(dest) in callDownloadFile without confining the destination. An attacker who influences arguments through an AI agent driving kubeshark mcp can write Hub-supplied bytes to any path writable by the local MCP user and can read captured network traffic from default auth-disabled Hub deployments. The tool is registered without --allow-destructive; reliable code execution is not demonstrated because the bytes are constrained to Hub API responses. Hub-side default authentication remains outside this remediation, so captured traffic can remain readable in default auth-disabled Hub deployments after the local destination-write fix. The destination-write issue is fixed in version 53.4.0.

Kubeshark is an eBPF-powered network observability tool for Kubernetes. From 53.1.0 until 53.4.0, the start_kubeshark MCP tool in cmd/mcpRunner.go uses callStartKubeshark to append caller-controlled pod_regex as a bare positional argument to kubeshark tap without a -- end-of-options separator, allowing a value beginning with --set to be parsed as a Helm value override. An attacker who influences tool arguments against kubeshark mcp --allow-destructive can redirect the privileged worker, Hub, and front images through tap.docker.registry and tap.docker.tag to an attacker-controlled registry. Because the deployed worker DaemonSet runs privileged with host networking and host filesystem access, a malicious image can obtain node and cluster-admin access when the host already has permission to deploy it. This issue is fixed in version 53.4.0.

Due to a Debian-specific patch, the directory used to share data between the
LightDM and the users logging in was writable by the lightdm user of the
unprivileged greeter process. A process running under the lightdm identity
could leverage write access to that directory to force the LightDM process
(running as root) to change ownership and permissions on other root-owned
directories and escalate privileges from the lightdm user to root.

A vulnerability was detected in hrshadhin CloudSchool up to 3.0.1. This affects an unknown function of the file app/Http/Controllers/Backend/EventController.php of the component Event Description Handler. The manipulation of the argument data results in cross site scripting. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A weakness has been identified in Mereithhh VanBlog up to 0.54.0. This affects an unknown part of the file packages/server/src/types/access/access.ts of the component Image Upload Endpoint. Executing a manipulation can lead to cross site scripting. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been made available to the public and could be used for attacks. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

A security vulnerability has been detected in sox_ng up to 14.8.1. Affected by this issue is the function read_samples_voc of the file src/voc.c of the component VOC Decoder. Such manipulation leads to out-of-bounds write. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit has been disclosed publicly and may be used. The name of the patch is 0b40408b. A patch should be applied to remediate this issue. The vendor was contacted early, responded in a very professional manner and quickly released a fixed version of the affected product.

External control of a file path in Amazon Deep Java Library (DJL) versions 0.7.0 through 0.38.0 might allow a remote unauthenticated third party to read arbitrary files that the library process can access. To do this, the third party supplies a crafted model archive.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to version 0.39.0 or later.
The Patch Management Engine in N-central is vulnerable to LPE via attacker controlled metadata

mail-parser is a tool that parses emails by enhancing the Python standard library and extracting message details into a comprehensive object. Prior to 4.6.2, multiple message-processing behaviors can raise exceptions or silently lose content. Headers colliding with methods such as Parse, Message, and Write_Attachments can place bound method objects into parsed output and raise TypeError when a caller requests JSON serialization such as mail_json. When byte input is parsed through parse_from_bytes(), an 8-bit header value returned as email.header.Header can likewise raise TypeError when an X_raw accessor passes the value to json.dumps; both exceptions are outside the MailParserError hierarchy. Separately, rewritten names such as Subject_json and X_Spam_Flag can be substituted or disappear from mail, headers, and JSON output while has_defects remains false, and a headerless message can be treated as falsy before parser state is initialized, causing body and attachment properties to return empty values without an error signal. These behaviors can abort message processing or hide malicious indicators from downstream scanners. This issue is fixed in version 4.6.2.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 3.5.0 until 3.13.0, built-in penetration-detection patterns in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py execute through a direct pattern.search(content) call instead of the timeout-protected create_safe_matcher() path used for custom patterns. The built-in template-injection detector contains an unbounded expression with quadratic behavior when scanning repeated opening braces. Because penetration detection and enhanced mode are enabled by a stock SecurityConfig, an unauthenticated request can block the shared asyncio event loop, affecting all application endpoints. The triggering input does not produce a detection match, so the request can complete without incrementing ban counters or being recorded as suspicious. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, ContentPreprocessor.preprocess() in guard_core/detection_engine/preprocessor.py collapses all whitespace before built-in pattern matching in the default enhanced mode. This removes carriage returns and newlines required by the http_split and newline-anchored cmd_injection detectors in guard_core/handlers/suspatterns_handler.py, making those detectors unable to match. Framework-decoded CRLF can therefore pass through Guard Core unflagged while the downstream application still receives the raw newline-bearing value. Direct security impact requires a downstream stack or application that persists or re-emits the value into a CRLF-tolerant response or command context. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

Guard Core is an API security core engine for the FastAPI-Guard, FlaskAPI Guard, and DjAPI Guard adapters. From 1.0.0 until 3.13.0, _extract_from_forwarded_header() in guard_core/utils.py returns the selected X-Forwarded-For entry without validating that it is an IP address. In deployments configured with trusted_proxies where the selected entry is attacker-controlled, the arbitrary client_ip string reaches BehaviorTracker in guard_core/handlers/behavior_handler.py and is interpolated into Redis key names and blocking KEYS glob patterns. Glob metacharacters can cause one request to count other clients' behavior events, embedded separators can disturb key parsing, and rotating identities can create unbounded keys while repeatedly scanning the shared Redis keyspace. A non-IP identity can also reach a ban action and cause an uncaught validation error. This issue is fixed in version 3.13.0.

libspdm is a sample implementation that follows the DMTF SPDM specifications. Prior to 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2, libspdm_x509_verify_cert_chain() in os_stub/cryptlib_openssl/pk/x509.c and os_stub/cryptlib_mbedtls/pk/x509.c validates certificate signatures one link at a time instead of validating the complete X.509 path. In deployments using a pinned root with a constrained multi-tier PKI, an attacker holding a valid issuer credential below a constrained CA can present a subordinate certificate that exceeds pathLenConstraint or nameConstraints and may be accepted for SPDM identity validation. Exploitation requires the application to use libspdm's backend validation without an additional certificate-chain validation mechanism, the pinned root cannot be substituted, and the deployment's measurement policy must allow identity impersonation alone to satisfy its acceptance requirements. The mbedTLS backend remains unable to enforce nameConstraints because upstream mbedTLS does not implement that check. The full-chain validation changes are released in versions 3.8.3 and 4.0.0-rc2.

create-ecdh is a browserifiable implementation of Node.js crypto.createECDH. In versions 4.0.4 and below, the JavaScript implementation (browser.js, used by browser bundlers and on Node.js versions without a working native crypto.createECDH) did not validate peer public keys in ECDH.prototype.computeSecret or ECDH.prototype.setPublicKey. The peer point was multiplied by the local private key without checking that it was on the configured curve or in its prime-order subgroup. An attacker who can submit public keys to a party that reuses a static private key can perform an invalid-curve or small-subgroup attack and recover the private key modulo small factors, eventually recovering the full key via the Chinese Remainder Theorem. For the ed25519 and curve25519 curves, low-order points were also accepted, which could force a predictable shared secret. On modern Node.js, create-ecdh re-exports the native implementation, which is not affected. This issue is fixed in version 4.0.5.

The shiro:principal tags in shiro-web (Jakarta Pages) and shiro-jakarta-ee (Jakarta Faces) did not escape their output, which could allow cross-site scripting when a principal value is not fully trusted.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when the principal tag is used.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which escapes the output.
Alternatively, validate principal values on input.

Git over HTTP lowers the required permission for pushes to read access, so that the AGit flow works, and relies on the repository's server-side hooks to enforce write access. A repository that is still being created by a migration, fork or template generation has no hooks yet, so a user with read access to it could push branches and tags during that window, or after a failed migration that left the repository in that state. Git over HTTP now refuses requests to repositories that are still being created.

The web endpoint that removes an attachment skipped the permission check when the request came from the user who had uploaded the attachment, and it was reachable with read access to issues or pull requests. A user who had uploaded a release asset could still delete it after losing write access to the repository. The endpoint now only deletes attachments that the user uploaded and that are not yet linked to an issue, comment or release.

`DefaultPasswordService` and `SimpleCredentialsMatcher` could treat an empty stored credential as a match for an empty submitted password.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when accounts with an empty stored credential exist.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, avoid storing empty credentials, and reject empty passwords in the application.

When PropertiesRealm reloads its properties file, removed users and narrowed permissions could remain in effect.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.1, only when PropertiesRealm`loads its properties from a file, which is reloaded periodically by default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.2 or later, which fixes the issue.
Alternatively, restart the application after removing users or narrowing permissions.

When authentication caching is enabled on DefaultLdapRealm, after a user logs in successfully once, subsequent logins for that user succeed with any password.
A cached authentication skips the LDAP bind, and the AllowAllCredentialsMatcher installed by default in DefaultLdapRealm accepts any credentials, allowing an attacker who knows a valid username to authenticate as that user.
This issue affects all Apache Shiro versions through 3.0.0, only when using DefaultLdapRealm (or JndiLdapRealm) with authenticationCachingEnabled set to true, which is not the default.

Mitigation: Upgrade to version 3.0.1 or later, which fixes the issue by no longer installing AllowAllCredentialsMatcher by default.
Alternatively, disable authentication caching on the LDAP realm (this is the default), or configure a credentials matcher, such as SimpleCredentialsMatcher, that verifies credentials against the cached authentication info.

A vulnerability was detected in D-Link DIR-600L 2.17/2.17b02. Affected by this vulnerability is the function authenticationcgi_main of the file authentication.cgi. Performing a manipulation of the argument id/password results in stack-based buffer overflow. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit is now public and may be used.

A vulnerability was determined in Linux Foundation Magma up to 1.9.0. This issue affects the function hostOrgMiddleware of the file nms/server/host/middleware.ts of the component Host Middleware. This manipulation of the argument role causes missing authorization. It is possible to initiate the attack remotely. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized. The vendor was contacted early about this disclosure but did not respond in any way.

Frappe india-payroll before 16.0.4 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the get_employee_details, compute_tax_comparison and set_tax_regime methods of tax_regime_selector.py that allows authenticated low-privileged users to access other employees' payroll data. Attackers can supply another employee identifier to read base pay and earning and deduction components, or change the tax regime on draft Salary Structure Assignments to affect tax withholding.

Axeloz Filesharing before 2.14.3 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by storing raw HTML or javascript: Markdown links in bundle descriptions. Recipients viewing the public bundle preview page execute the script via Alpine x-html, letting attackers steal the owner_token from localStorage and issue owner-scoped requests against victim bundles.

Dokploy before 0.31.1 contains an OS command injection vulnerability in getComposeContainerCommand() that allows authenticated organization members to execute shell commands via the serviceName parameter. Attackers can store serviceName values with shell metacharacters through backup.create or backup.update tRPC procedures, executing commands as root when scheduled backups run and taking over the host via the mounted Docker socket.

A vulnerability was determined in itsourcecode Airline Reservation System 1.0. The impacted element is an unknown function of the file /admin/manage_user.php. This manipulation of the argument ID causes sql injection. Remote exploitation of the attack is possible. The exploit has been publicly disclosed and may be utilized.

A vulnerability was identified in D-Link DSL-6740C 20131126. This affects an unknown function of the file /etc/templates/ftpd/ftpd_conf.php of the component FTP Daemon. Such manipulation leads to hard-coded credentials. The attack can be executed remotely. The exploit is publicly available and might be used.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability in the /dbml/svg endpoint that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject javascript: hyperlinks by supplying crafted DBML table url, headercolor, or TableGroup color settings. Attackers can send a crafted SVG link that, when opened and the table header clicked, executes attacker JavaScript in the Kroki origin.

Deserialization of Untrusted Data in Apache Roller versions 4.0.0 through 6.1.4 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary code. The XML-RPC endpoint accepts vendor extension types and deserializes them before authenticating the requester.

This is the same vulnerability as CVE-2026-82384, which listed only Apache Roller 6.1.5 as affected. This issue is being actively exploited.

Users are recommended to upgrade to Apache Roller 6.1.6 or later, which disables the extension types and rejects XML-RPC requests when the XML-RPC feature is disabled.

Users who cannot upgrade right away should set "enabledForExtensions" to "false" in WEB-INF/web.xml, or remove the "/roller-services/xmlrpc" servlet mapping, and restart Roller. Disabling XML-RPC in the administration UI is not enough, because older versions deserialize the request before checking that setting.

A vulnerability was detected in DrayTek Vigor2960 1.5.1.6. Affected by this issue is the function sub_1E084 of the file /cgi-bin/mainfunction.cgi?action=doWebBackup. The manipulation of the argument option results in path traversal. It is possible to launch the attack remotely. The exploit is now public and may be used. Upgrading to version 1.5.1.7 can resolve this issue. You should upgrade the affected component. The vendor recommends: "1.5.1.6 isn't the latest version of 2960, the latest version fixes many security issues. And we have another one in our release plan which should solve the issues reported."

Zr.Admin.NET commit 85cff6a through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in GET /workflow/instance/{instanceId} that lets logged-in users view others' workflow instances. Authenticated low-privilege attackers can enumerate sequential instance IDs to read other users' approval requests, including submitted form contents, applicant details and approval records.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 0ee1ab8 through commit eb9228a contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows any logged-in user to read arbitrary server files via the path parameter of /common/DownloadFile. Attackers can supply absolute paths or ../ sequences to read appsettings files and use the JwtSettings SecretKey to forge administrator tokens.

Zr.Admin.NET commit af07ffc through commit eb9228a contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in SysProfileController.UpdateProfile that allows any authenticated user to modify other accounts via UserId. Attackers can set the administrator's phone number to one they control, request an SMS code via /checkMobile, and log in through /PhoneLogin to take over the administrator account.

Zr.Admin.NET commit 1845017 through commit eb9228a contains a missing authorization vulnerability in TasksController.Get that allows any logged-in user to read scheduled task details without the monitor:job permission. Attackers can obtain task ids from the unprotected /monitor/jobLog/list endpoint and retrieve job parameters, API URLs, cron expressions, and stored SQL statements.

Netcccyun dnsmgr 2.18 before 2.22 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in POST /cloudflare/get_domain_default_line that allows restricted users to access domains outside their permissions. Restricted sub-users or single-domain logins can iterate the domain_id parameter to enumerate panel domain ids and read each domain's DNS line list and default line.

Course-tencent-cloud before 2.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view other users' refund previews by supplying an order sn to /api/refund/confirm. Attackers can compute valid sn values from Sqids-encoded sequential order ids using the default key to disclose ordered items, prices, refund amounts, fees and deadlines.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the glTF and glTF2 importers that allows attackers to read local files via crafted buffers[].uri values. Attackers can supply glTF models with '..' segments or absolute paths in buffer URIs to load files like /etc/passwd into imported mesh vertex data.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains an integer overflow vulnerability in OgreBinarySerializer::ReadSubMesh that allows attackers to crash applications by supplying crafted Ogre binary .mesh files. Attackers can set a large index count so the 32-bit buffer size wraps, causing a segmentation fault in aiMesh::~aiMesh() during scene teardown.

Assimp through 6.0.6 contains a heap out-of-bounds read vulnerability in MD2Importer::InternReadFile that allows attackers to read past the file buffer via an unvalidated stored frameSize header field. Attackers can supply a crafted .md2 file loaded with a non-zero keyframe selected to crash the application or leak adjacent heap memory into the imported mesh.

OkHttp through 5.5.1 contains an improper certificate validation vulnerability in CertificatePinner that skips pin checks because Pin.matchesHostname does not normalize trailing-dot hostnames. Network attackers with a CA-trusted certificate not matching configured pins can intercept or modify TLS traffic when applications request the trailing-dot form of pinned hosts.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject scripts via unvalidated svg-color-dark-scheme and svg-color-light-scheme options. Attackers can craft a GET /goat/svg URL whose option value closes the SVG style element, executing JavaScript in the Kroki origin when victims open it.

Kroki before 0.36.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the BlockDiag family of engines that allows unauthenticated attackers to make server requests via node icon and background attributes. Attackers can send crafted diagrams to POST /blockdiag/svg or sibling endpoints to query internal services or cloud metadata and read local image files from the server.

littlefs through 2.11.3, when built with LFS_MIGRATE, contains a type confusion vulnerability in lfs_dir_traverse() that treats a stack lfs_diskoff struct as an lfs_attr array. Attackers can supply a crafted littlefs v1 image whose metadata is read as LFS_FROM_USERATTRS during migration, causing out-of-bounds stack reads and process crashes.

Qbian61 forum-java commit 20f7e68 through commit 63152c4 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows authenticated users to inject script by posting unsanitized comment content rendered via jQuery .html() in the reply dialog. Attackers can post comments with img onerror payloads that execute when victims click Reply, stealing the non-HttpOnly sid session cookie to hijack accounts including administrators.

Bolo (bolo-solo) 1.7 through 2.6.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to read article view passwords via the public GET /articles endpoint. Attackers can retrieve the plaintext articleViewPwd field returned by ArticleProcessor.getArticlesByPage and submit it to read password-protected article content.

Several endpoints that work on both issues and pull requests did not check which of the two the addressed item is. A user who can read a repository's issues but not its pull requests could read pull request data through the issue sub-resources of the API (timeline, attachments, labels, subscriptions, tracked times and reactions), and list pull requests through the repository's issue search and milestone pages; the same applied in the other direction. These endpoints now check read access to the unit the item belongs to. The API endpoints were fixed in 28.2.0 and 28.3.0, the search and milestone pages in 28.4.0.

SSCMS 7.2.0 through 7.4.0 contains an arbitrary file read vulnerability that allows any registered user-center account to copy server files by supplying source paths to the layerImageUpload endpoint. Attackers can send siteId 0 with crafted filePaths entries to copy configuration files into their public sitefiles/home upload directory and download them anonymously.

EdgeChat 2.5.0 through 2.21.0 contains a cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows invited users to inject HTML through unescaped usernames in the Vditor @-mention autocomplete. Attackers can register with a username containing an img onerror payload that executes when mentioned, stealing the localStorage session token to take over victim accounts.
Files or directories accessible to external parties vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Probe System Files.
Access of resource using incompatible type ('type confusion') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source Starfish allows Input Data Manipulation.

Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated read-only users to retrieve Git deployment credentials via documentation API responses. Attackers can query GET /kal-api/docs/documentations or POST /kal-api/docs/documentation to obtain plaintext gitUser and gitPassword values and authenticate to external Git repositories.

Kalmia through 0.2.0 contains a stored cross-site scripting vulnerability that allows read-only authenticated users to upload HTML or SVG files via the upload-file endpoint without type restrictions. Attackers can share links to files served unauthenticated through the file get route, executing JavaScript in the admin origin to steal administrator JWTs from localStorage.
Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow') vulnerability in Samsung Open Source mTower allows Overflow Buffers.

The httpx Ruby gem parses JSON response bodies through its transcoder layer. HTTPX::Response#json delegates to Transcoder::JSON.decode, and when the oj gem is loaded and multi_json is absent, the decoder falls back to json_load, which calls Oj.load(response.to_s) with no mode option. Oj.load defaults to :object mode, in which a response document can allocate any already-loaded Ruby class ("^o":"ClassName") and set its instance variables, or resolve a class or module reference ("^c":"Name"). An attacker who controls, or can influence, the URL an application fetches with HTTPX.get(url).json therefore controls object instantiation in the victim process. With a matching gadget chain, this issue can potentially cause remote code execution. Affects httpx 1.9.0; fixed in 1.9.1.

LimeSurvey before 6.17.16+260814 and 7.x before 7.0.10+260813 contains an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability in the public statistics page via POST parameter names. Attackers can submit backtick-containing parameter names to buildSelects() and use blind techniques to read administrator password hashes and survey responses on MySQL or MariaDB.

RedAmon 4.0.0 before 7.8.0 contains a missing object-level authorization vulnerability that allows authenticated users to control other tenants' agent sessions by supplying arbitrary session ids. Attackers can call /api/agent/sessions, interact and kill routes to list, kill, or send commands into other users' meterpreter and shell sessions on their compromised targets.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.1 contain a heap buffer overflow in ReadBinaryData() in jxrgluelib/JXRMeta.c caused by integer overflow of the metadata count. Attackers can supply a JPEG XR file with a count of 0xFFFFFFFE or 0xFFFFFFFF, wrapping PKAlloc(uCount + 2) to an undersized buffer that the following file read overflows, corrupting heap memory in decoding applications.

Microsoft jxrlib through 1.1 and the mircomir jxrlib fork before 1.3.6 contain a stack buffer over-read vulnerability in ReadWMIHeader() in image/decode/strdec.c due to an unterminated signature buffer. Attackers can supply a crafted JPEG XR file whose 8 signature bytes contain no zero byte, causing strstr to read past the stack buffer and potentially crash the application.

@tinacms/graphql 2.2.2 through 4.1.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write files outside the content root by following pre-existing dangling symlinks. Attackers can create documents through the GraphQL API targeting a dangling symlink, bypassing assertWithinBase checks, to write controlled content such as authorized_keys to server-writable locations.

Koillection before 1.8.6 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to view objects nested under private parents through the shared search autocomplete route. Attackers can query GET /user/{username}/search/autocomplete/{term}, whose native SQL filters on visibility instead of final_visibility, to obtain names, ids and counts of hidden collections, items, albums and wishlists.

Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in DataSourceController.testConnect that allows any authenticated user to open arbitrary JDBC connections by supplying caller-controlled connection settings. Attackers can probe internal hosts and ports via returned driver errors, or supply a MySQL JDBC URL enabling local-infile against a malicious server to read files from the Dinky host.

Dinky through 1.2.5 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in ClusterConfigurationController that allows authenticated users without cluster configuration permissions to list Flink cluster configurations. Attackers can query the /api/clusterConfiguration/list and listAll endpoints to retrieve full configJson deployment settings for every cluster in their tenant.

REBUILD 4.3.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to obtain a SYSTEM_USER token by requesting /commons/file-preview with an arbitrary src value. Attackers can read the leaked _csrfToken from the redirect Location header and send it as X-AuthToken to access the admin center and administrative APIs.

REBUILD 3.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains a privilege escalation vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to modify their own roleId through mass assignment in /app/entity/record-save and /app/entity/common-save. Attackers can submit their own User record with roleId set to the built-in administrator role, bypassing updatable=false restrictions to gain full administrator privileges.

REBUILD 4.5.0 through 4.5.4 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows low-privileged authenticated users to recover the administrator password hash by filtering User.password through the MCP QueryRecords tool. Attackers can send LK2 prefix-match filters to the /gw/mcp/sse gateway and use the returned total count as an oracle to extract the SHA-256 hash one character at a time, then log in as administrator.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in ReportGenerator.generate_task_report that allows registered users to read server files and perform SSRF. Attackers can create a project whose name contains a link attachment element and download the task PDF report to retrieve local files or internal network responses.

DeepAudit 2.0.0-beta.1 through 3.8.0 contains a path traversal vulnerability that allows authenticated users to write arbitrary files by importing projects with crafted IDs. Attackers can set absolute or ../ project IDs via /api/v1/database/import, then upload ZIPs through /api/v1/scan/upload-zip following cloned symlinks to overwrite app/main.py for remote code execution.

Weblate 2026.6 through 2026.11.2 contains an information disclosure vulnerability in ChangeManager.last_changes() that exposes workspaces the viewer cannot view by skipping Workspace.can_view() checks site-wide. Anonymous visitors on instances with REQUIRE_LOGIN disabled and only public projects can query /changes/, /api/changes/, or RSS/CSV feeds to obtain hidden workspace names, UUIDs, actions, and timestamps.

Kiwi TCMS before 17.1 contains a hard-coded cryptographic key vulnerability that allows remote attackers to forge signed data by using the publicly known Django SECRET_KEY in tcms/settings/common.py. Attackers can forge or tamper with signed cookie-based messages and django.core.signing payloads, weakening password-reset and session-authentication HMACs on deployments keeping the default.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an open redirect vulnerability that allows remote attackers to send users to arbitrary sites by supplying an unvalidated redirectUri parameter on the /pay/[id] payment link page. Attackers can distribute payment links with a malicious redirectUri that PayPageWidget opens via window.open after payment without noopener, enabling phishing and reverse tabnabbing of the payment page.

Unrolled Secure before 1.18.0 contains an SSLRedirect bypass vulnerability in Secure.isSSL() that trusts the client-supplied r.URL.Scheme to determine HTTPS transport. Attackers can send plaintext HTTP requests with an absolute-form https:// request-target to skip the HTTPS redirect and have application responses served unencrypted.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in revalidatePathAction and revalidateCacheTagAction server actions in revalidate.ts. Unauthenticated attackers can use action identifiers exposed in the client bundle to send POST requests that purge cached pages and data, forcing repeated regeneration and degrading performance.

thirdweb Dashboard through commit 940b3745 contains an information disclosure vulnerability that allows authenticated users to read non-public team metadata by requesting the team join page with any invite ID. Attackers who know a team slug can obtain the serialized Team object, exposing billing email, billing status, Stripe customer ID, verified domain and support identifiers.

Keystatic through 0.6.9 contains a path traversal vulnerability in the getIsPathValid function that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to access sibling paths sharing a content directory name prefix. Attackers can send requests with a no-cors header to the blob, update, and tree handlers under /api/keystatic to read, create, overwrite, or delete files such as posts-evil/pwn.yaml.

Contentlayer @contentlayer/source-files through 0.3.4 contains a code injection vulnerability that allows attackers who control content files to execute JavaScript by abusing gray-matter's still-enabled JavaScript engine in parseMarkdown(). Attackers can start a Markdown or MDX file with a ---js or ---javascript frontmatter delimiter to run code during build, exposing CI build secrets.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains a rate limit bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to evade throttling by spoofing the X-Forwarded-For header, because trustProxy is enabled. Attackers can send X-Forwarded-For set to 127.0.0.1 or rotate values to brute-force the administrator password via POST /admin/login and evade comment IP blocklists.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an HTML injection vulnerability in linesToEmailContent() that allows unauthenticated attackers to inject markup into notification emails because comment content is not escaped. Attackers can post comments or replies via POST /comments containing forged links, images, or tracking resources rendered in administrator and author mail clients from the blog's address.

NodePress through 8.5.1 contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to gain administrator access by using the hardcoded default password 'root'. Attackers can send base64-encoded 'root' to POST /admin/login when NP_ADMIN_DEFAULT_PASSWORD is unset to obtain admin tokens and fully control the site.

Sandboxie-Plus before 1.18.6 contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability in SbieSvc that allows standard users to launch UpdUtil.exe as SYSTEM via MSGID_PROCESS_RUN_UPDATER requests. Attackers can inject code into a signed SandMan.exe process to bypass the signature check and write attacker-controlled files to arbitrary paths, achieving SYSTEM code execution.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.0.0 before 9.2.1 contains a path traversal vulnerability in back-office theme and module archive import that allows authenticated employees to write files outside intended directories. Attackers can craft a theme name in config/theme.yml or upload a module archive extracted before validation to place PHP files in web-accessible locations and execute code.

GPAC before 26.07.0 contains a NULL pointer dereference vulnerability in gf_node_get_tag() that allows attackers to crash the process via crafted XMT connect elements. Attackers can supply an XMT scene file whose connect element has a parent with no node, crashing MP4Box during processing and causing denial of service.

msgpack-c through 7.0.2 contains a heap buffer overflow vulnerability in msgpack_vrefbuffer_migrate() in src/vrefbuffer.c that checks capacity against the source array's end pointer. When migrating between vrefbuffers of unequal size, the realloc is skipped and memcpy() writes iovec entries past the destination array, corrupting adjacent heap memory or crashing the application.

Alinto SOGo before 5.12.13 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in SQLSource contact lookup that allows authenticated users to inject SQL by placing a backslash before a quote in the object name. Attackers can send requests under a SQL-backed address book path on MySQL or MariaDB to perform UNION or boolean-based reads of the user-source table, including password hashes.

7-Zip File Manager before 26.03 fails to detect archive entry names padded with Unicode space characters, allowing attackers to bypass the deceptive file name warning in CPanel::IsVirus_Message. Attackers can craft archive entries like a PDF name followed by ideographic spaces and .hta to hide the real extension, executing script content via ShellExecuteExW when opened.

Umbraco CMS 17.0.0 before 17.7.1 and 18.0.0 before 18.2.1 contains an authorization bypass vulnerability in Management API document version endpoints that skip per-document ContentPermissionByResource checks. Authenticated back-office users restricted to a start node can list and read document versions outside their tree by GUID, exposing unpublished values and altering prevent-cleanup flags.

Frappe Framework before 15.123.0 and 16.x before 16.50.0 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the frappe.email.email_body.get_email_html method, which lacks role checks. Authenticated users, including portal Website Users, can inject stylesheet link tags into unescaped email templates, causing Premailer to fetch internal or external hosts and return the content.

Ghost by muneeb141 on the main branch from commit c731cdf through commit 672dfec contains an authentication bypass vulnerability in the whitelisted ghost.api.ghost.convert_to_real_user method that allows unauthenticated attackers to skip OTP verification by setting the client-supplied bypass_otp parameter. Attackers can obtain a ghost session from the guest-accessible create_ghost_session endpoint, then call convert_to_real_user with an arbitrary real_email and bypass_otp=1 to receive OAuth tokens for existing accounts and take them over.

TridotsTech go1cms master branch through commit 7f68d05 and version-3 branch before commit ead8da3 contains a missing authentication vulnerability in the guest-whitelisted update_doc method that allows unauthenticated attackers to modify any document. Attackers can supply a doctype, name and arbitrary fields that are saved with ignore_permissions=True, altering User records to escalate privileges, take over accounts or tamper with business data.

Cloud Commander (cloudcmd) before 19.21.4 contains an authentication bypass and path traversal vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to rename files by sending PUT /rename requests handled before authentication middleware. Attackers can supply absolute or ../ paths in the from and to arrays to move any file the Node.js process can access outside the configured root, causing data loss or denial of service.

CBoard before commit 7bd8180 contains a missing authorization vulnerability that allows any authenticated user to reach admin functions because AdminController and DashboardController methods bypass AOP role checks. Attackers with no role grants can call deleteUser, deleteRole, getUserList, getAllWidgetList and getAllDatasetList to read query configurations and delete accounts including the administrator.

free5GC WebConsole through 1.4.6 contains an authorization flaw in the ChangePasswordInfo handler that allows authenticated tenant users to change other members' passwords. Attackers can send POST /api/change-password with another tenant member's email and a new password, without the current password, to take over that account.

SplitPro through 2.1.6 contains a missing authorization vulnerability in the addOrEditExpense and addOrEditCurrencyConversion tRPC mutations that allows authenticated users to assign expenses to arbitrary users. Attackers can enumerate sequential user IDs and supply them in participants or paidBy fields to fabricate debts on victims' balances, even in unseen groups.

crw-server before 0.45.1 contains a server-side request forgery vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to reach internal services by supplying an unvalidated baseUrl to the /v1/scrape endpoint. Attackers can set llmApiKey and request the summary format, making the server POST to loopback or private addresses and use returned warnings as a reachability oracle.

django-tenants 3.4.8 before 4.0.1 contains an SQL injection vulnerability in its PostgreSQL backend that allows attackers to inject SQL through unescaped tenant schema names. Attackers who can choose or influence a schema name can supply quote characters that are interpolated into SET search_path and CREATE, DROP or ALTER SCHEMA statements, letting them read other tenants' data or run SQL as the application's database user.

Chyrp Lite (xenocrat/chyrp-lite) contains a missing brute-force protection vulnerability in the main_login() function that allows remote attackers to repeatedly submit login attempts against the admin account without any attempt counter, lockout, delay, or CAPTCHA enforcement. Attackers can send unlimited password guesses via POST requests to the login action until a correct credential is found, gaining full administrative control including post publishing, user management, and file uploads.

In Open Object Rexx (ooRexx) before 5.2.0, RXAPI has a heap buffer over-read in a QueueManager DataQueue::addmethod. In particular, the code blindly trusts the message.parameter1 value provided by the client as the size used to fill the data from the queueData heap buffer. An attacker sends a large parameter1 value in an ADD_TO_SESSION_QUEUE or ADD_TO_NAMED_QUEUE message and then retrieves data with a PULL_FROM_SESSION_QUEUE message. (A very large value causes a process crash.)
